transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um... nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because... well, I've been dealing with some things at work. I direct a music ensemble. And for almost two years now, ever since this one commission we did, I just... I can't shake the certainty that a few people in the group are quietly undermining my work. 

It's... things like schedule changes, seating choices, little comments in rehearsals. They'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... I know what they're doing. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
When they show you emails or notes that seem to explain those incidents, are you still completely certain they’re undermining you?

Yeah. I am. 

...The emails don't really change anything. Like I said, it's been almost two years since that commission, and I just... I can't shake the certainty that they're doing it. The notes they show me don't change what's actually happening.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
No. I haven't.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your thoughts or actions?
No. I... no. My thoughts are my own. It's just... what I see them doing, that's all.
Outside of this situation at work, do you generally find yourself mistrusting other people’s motives?
No, not really. Just them. I don't... I don't have a problem with anyone else.
Do you believe for certain that these coworkers are deliberately trying to harm your career?

Yes. I... I am certain. For almost two years now, ever since the commission, I just... I can't shake it. A few people in the ensemble, they... they use schedule changes, seating choices, little comments in rehearsals... just to quietly undermine my work. They try to show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all, but... I know what they're doing.
Do you believe these coworkers are communicating special messages to you through things like the seating arrangements or comments in rehearsal?
No. I... no, not messages. It's not like that. They're just... doing what I said. Just making it hard for me to do my job.
Aside from this belief about your coworkers, have you had any other unusual experiences or symptoms?

No. Nothing else. Outside of this issue with the ensemble... things are fine. I still meet my deadlines. Keep up with my composing. I run most mornings. Things at home with my wife are... basically steady. That's it.
If someone you trust completely told you there is no plot against you at work, would you still be certain your coworkers are undermining you?

I... yes. I would still be certain. It doesn't matter who says it. I know what I see. I've lived with this for almost two years. Ever since that commission, it's just... I see the schedule changes. I see the seating choices. The little comments during rehearsals. They try to show me emails or notes to explain it away, but... I know they are undermining me. I just know it.
Do you believe your coworkers are doing anything to undermine you that would be impossible in ordinary life?
No. I don't... no. It's just ordinary things. Nothing impossible, if that's what you mean. Just... people being difficult. Like I said before.
Did this belief about your coworkers begin suddenly?
I... I wouldn't say suddenly. No. Just... over time, I guess. Gradually.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
No. No one has ever said that to me.
Has this situation at work caused a clear decline in how well you function in your job?

No. I haven't... I haven't lost any work or anything. I'm still taking care of myself. It's just... maybe rehearsals and, um, professional emails take a bit more energy right now. I just find myself rereading things, or... sometimes I have to ask for extra clarification on decisions. But that's it. I'm still doing my job.
Have you noticed yourself becoming emotionally flat or less able to feel or show emotions?
No. I... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that.
Did this start shortly after a very stressful event?
No. Um... I don't think so. Not that I can think of, anyway. Things were just... normal.
Have you ever believed that other people could read your thoughts?
No. Um... no. I've never thought anything like that.
Has this belief that your coworkers are undermining you been present continuously for more than three months?
Yeah. Um... it's been longer than that. It started after I won a commission... and they invited me to conduct the premiere. That was about a year and nine months ago.
Do you believe your coworkers have any supernatural, technological, or otherwise impossible way of undermining you?
No. Um... no. Nothing like that. Just... normal ways.
